$comment: Severity 1-5 with explicit operational triggers. Triage assigns severity by matching candidate signal against trigger. Convergence score uses these as inputs.

levels.label: Routine
levels.trigger: Baseline volatility within climatological or operational norms; no operational disruption; insurance / freight rates at baseline.
examples: Hurricane season start within +/- 2 weeks of climatological norm
Routine port-worker collective bargaining without strike authorization

levels.label: Elevated
levels.trigger: Heightened rhetoric, limited incidents (<=2 in 30 days), no measurable flow impact, premium <0.5% hull value.
examples: Above-normal seasonal outlook from issuing agency (e.g., NOAA +60% Atlantic)
Strike authorization vote passed but no strike date set

levels.label: Concerning
levels.trigger: Operational disruption visible — delays >24h average, queues forming, premium 0.5-1.0% hull value, >=3 incidents in 30 days, or a port restriction in force.
examples: Active tropical storm tracking toward landfall in T-72h
Strike action affecting one major port
Force-majeure declared on one major commodity stream

levels.label: Severe
levels.trigger: Sustained multi-front escalation — >30% volume reduction on the relevant flow OR alternative routes activated under stress; mediation channel still open; insurance >1.0% hull value.
examples: Cat-3+ hurricane landfall on energy hub
Major FM cascade across an industry

levels.label: Crisis
levels.trigger: Sustained de-facto closure (>80% volume reduction sustained >=7 days) AND any of: (a) formal closure announcement, (b) confirmed strike on critical infra, (c) alternative-route saturation forcing rationing on a refined-product class, (d) insurance unobtainable or >5%, (e) public collapse of mediation channel with no successor.
examples: Cat-5 direct hit on Houston refining complex with sustained outage
Multi-week sustained shipping shutdown at a global chokepoint
